title: Quasi-compact and quasi-separated permanence for algebraic stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of morphisms in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. An algebraic stack is quasi-separated when its absolute diagonal $\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the product and diagonal use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $\mathcal Y$ is quasi-separated, then $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Neither stack need be Deligne--Mumford, Noetherian or of finite type, and $f$ need not be representable.

proof.text: View the stacks absolutely over $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers]: $j_!\mathcal X$ and $j_!\mathcal Y$ are algebraic stacks over $B$, $j_!\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact, the absolute products and diagonals of the statement are those over $B$, and $2$-fibre products are unchanged; we write $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,f$ for $j_!\mathcal X,j_!\mathcal Y,j_!f$. Let $p:\mathcal X\to B$ and $g:\mathcal Y\to B$ be their structure morphisms, so $g\circ f\simeq p$. The source is quasi-compact, hence [lem-sfb-stack-quasicompact-absolute-criterion] makes $p$ quasi-compact. The absolute quasi-separatedness hypotheses say exactly that $p$ is quasi-separated and that $\Delta_g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated on algebraic-space scheme tests. The scheme-test/stack-test equivalence [lem-sfb-representable-stack-quasicompact-tests] therefore makes $\Delta_g$ a quasi-compact stack morphism.

source.place: Tag 075S (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), proof of (1) and (2); Tag 04YW (definition-separated), clause (4). algebraic.tex Tag 04X5 (lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme) for viewing the stacks over Spec Z.

proof.text: Form $P=\mathcal X\times_B\mathcal Y$, an algebraic stack by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Factor $f$ as $\mathcal X\xrightarrow{\gamma}P\xrightarrow{q}\mathcal Y$, with $\gamma(x)=(x,f(x))$. The square with top arrow $\gamma$, bottom arrow $\Delta_g:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y\times_B\mathcal Y$, and right arrow $(f\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2)$ is $2$-cartesian: its objects specify $(x,y,\alpha:f(x)\simeq y)$, and $(x,y,\alpha)$ is isomorphic to $(x,f(x),\mathrm{id})$, with arrows determined by the arrow of $x$. Thus $\gamma$ is a base change of the quasi-compact $\Delta_g$; $q$ is a base change of the quasi-compact $p$. For the definition in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], base change preserves quasi-compactness directly: testing a pullback at a quasi-compact $\mathcal T$ gives the original morphism tested at the composite $\mathcal T$-map. Composition preserves it directly too: first pull back $q$ at $\mathcal T$, obtaining a quasi-compact stack, then pull back $\gamma$ at that stack. Therefore $f=q\gamma$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 050Y (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence), graph factorization; Tags 050V and 050W, proved here directly from Tag 050U.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-quasiseparated-cancellation] to $\mathcal X\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal Y\xrightarrow{g}B$. Its first hypothesis holds because $gf\simeq p$ is quasi-separated; its second holds because $\Delta_g$ is quasi-separated by the absolute quasi-separatedness of $\mathcal Y$. It follows that $f$ is quasi-separated. Together with step 2, $j_!f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over $B$, so $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over $S$ by part (3) of [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers]. This proves the assertion.
